subject.title: [Bug]: Block streaming can drop paragraph separators across streamed updates

question: Should the permanent block-streaming contract preserve paragraph boundaries with explicit seam metadata/reserved-width splitting, or accept a narrower text-only common-case repair?
rationale: The source-proven bug has two candidate fixes, but the remaining maxChars boundary behavior affects the shared delivery contract and should be chosen by maintainers before closure.

options.title: Require a durable seam contract
options.body: Carry paragraph boundary semantics through an in-budget mechanism, such as explicit seam metadata or reserve-width splitting, and consolidate one candidate PR around that design.

options.title: Accept common-case text preservation
options.body: Land one current text-only candidate for ordinary paragraph boundaries while leaving the maxChars edge documented as remaining work.

options.title: Pause candidates for design first
options.body: Close or pause the competing PRs until the streaming payload contract is designed separately.

recommendation.title: Require a durable seam contract
recommendation.body: Carry paragraph boundary semantics through an in-budget mechanism, such as explicit seam metadata or reserve-width splitting, and consolidate one candidate PR around that design.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has strong history in block-reply coalescing and chunking hardening, making it the best available owner for the boundary-contract choice.
